statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES (orange). NQ is quoted at 28,841.25, down 1.86%, holding roughly eight points off a third consecutive lower low at 28,833.50. ES has joined at its own session low of 7,598.75 and the DAX has extended to 25,385.03, while VIX prints a session high of 18.00 and WTI a session high of 103.80. Two of the three counterweights that held the prior assessment inside the watch band have degraded: oil is extending rather than consolidating and the 10-year is no longer unchanged at 4.975%. The Dow-to-Nasdaq spread remains the one intact counterweight. Tail moves three points to 26 and crosses the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail at 26 sits in the elevated band, one point above the block threshold, so the mapped state is BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window now begins at the current hour and runs to 16:00 UTC, covering the European session, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours. Conditional Tail peaks at 29 in the first full cash hour and remains inside the block band throughout, six points below the strong-block threshold. From 17:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band and eases to the EA_ON mapping across the Asian hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ prints a third consecutive lower low at 28,833.50 and holds near it while ES joins at its own session low, VIX reaches 18.00 and WTI extends to 103.80; Tail crosses the block threshold at 26
body:
The structure that the prior two assessments described as forming is now observed. NQ is quoted at 28,841.25, down 545.75 points or 1.86% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 05:16 EDT. The session low has extended again, from 28,905.00 to 28,833.50, and the contract is trading about eight points above it, near 3% of a 28,833.50 to 29,111.00 range. That is the third consecutive lower low of this session, each one following a failed bounce. Repeated extension after failed retracements, with price holding at the session extreme, is the specific price path that denies a mean-reversion book the two-way trade it needs, and it is now observed rather than anticipated.

The move has also broadened. One hour ago the decline was carried almost entirely by the Nasdaq contract. ES is now 7,600.00, down 0.78%, and is itself sitting at a session low of 7,598.75, so the S&P contract is no longer merely lower but is holding its own extreme. The DAX has extended to 25,396.42, down 0.67%, with a fresh session low of 25,385.03, confirming and extending rather than merely joining. The VIX is 17.86, up 12.75% from a 15.84 close, and has printed a session high of 18.00.

Two of the three counterweights that held the prior assessment inside the watch band have degraded. WTI is 103.41, up 3.36%, and has extended to a new session high of 103.80, where an hour ago it was consolidating off its high inside an unchanged range; the energy leg is now confirming. The 10-year yield is 4.975%, up about three basis points on the day, where an hour ago it was described as unchanged; it now sits above the 4.95% H.15 print for 10 September rather than level with it. Neither move is large, and the three-basis-point shift in the 10-year is far from the aligned-yield signature present in this strategy's historical failures, but both have stopped arguing against the equity move.

One counterweight remains genuinely intact, and it is the reason this assessment stops at 26 rather than moving further. Dow futures are 52,852.00, down only 0.28%, against NQ's 1.86%. A spread of roughly 158 basis points between the Nasdaq and the Dow remains the signature of a sector de-rating rather than index-wide liquidation, and it leaves a large part of the market with capacity to absorb the story. The whole NQ range is still 277.5 points, under 1% of index value, built over roughly sixteen hours. This is a grinding, stair-stepped decline, not violent directional repricing, and a grind of that shape still offers mean reversion, at a slower cadence and from progressively lower levels.

The catalyst stack behind the move is unchanged and verified. Over the weekend the chief executives of the two leading frontier AI laboratories argued publicly for slowing the pace of capability improvement, and the OpenAI chief executive said a public listing this year would be ill-advised. Asia priced it first, with tech-heavy markets there falling between 1% and 3%. Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline, which had been carrying four to five million barrels a day, or 4% to 5% of global supply, was shut after a drone attack on 11 September, and Brent is near 107.18, up about 2.5% after gaining almost 9% last week. Into that, Reuters reports markets pricing a near-90% probability of a quarter-point policy increase on Wednesday, which would be the first since mid-2023.

Weighing the newly observed structure and the two degraded counterweights against the intact Dow spread and the narrow absolute range, Tail moves three points to 26. That crosses the block threshold by one point. The judgment is that observed repeated extension after failed retracements, with price at the extreme and three cross-asset legs now confirming, is materially more than the watch band should carry, while the sector-specific character of the move and the absence of an aligned curve argue against escalating further. Stress rises one point to 79, the top of the high band, describing a difficult but recoverable environment. Confidence holds at 88: live quotes for the index, ES, Dow futures, European cash, volatility, oil and the 10-year were obtained directly this hour, every material story was verified at a primary or reputable source, and one URL surfaced in search was checked and discarded as being from March rather than today. The only material gap is the shared cross-asset context file, which is both partial and roughly two and a quarter hours old this hour and whose breadth and megacap sections describe Friday's session rather than the current one, so it was not used as current confirmation.

Conditional risk is concentrated from the current hour through 16:00 UTC, with the 13:30 UTC cash open as the central checkpoint and a conditional peak of Tail 29 in the first full cash hour. Nothing about that auction is observed. The nearest conditional invalidation of the current structure is a reclaim of 29,000; the nearest confirmation would be a fourth lower low beneath 28,833.50 accompanied by shallow pullbacks.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail rose steadily through Sunday's European and US hours from 11 at 09:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16 at the 16:00 UTC handover, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Across the overnight session it was unusually stable, printing 20 in seven of the following nine hours with 19 at 02:00 and 06:00 UTC, before the European open lifted it to 21 at 07:00 UTC and 23 at 08:00 UTC. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first twelve hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the overnight session with two single-hour reversions to green. Dominant mode read normal through the Sunday hours, event/whipsaw for the reopen hour, and mixed for every hour from 23:00 UTC onward. Confidence fell from 86 to 71 around the 16:00 UTC handover, then rebuilt steadily to 88 as live overnight price-path evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk now begins at the current hour rather than at the cash open, because the block-band score is derived from structure already observed. The window runs to 16:00 UTC and covers the remaining European session, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours. The forecast holds at 26 through the deepest European liquidity, eases to the 25 boundary across the midday lull and premarket, then steps to 28 for the opening auction and peaks at 29 in the first full cash hour, the narrow single-hour top of the series. That peak is four points above the prior assessment's projection because a third lower low, a broadening into ES and two degraded cross-asset counterweights have since been observed. The peak stays inside the block band and six points below the strong-block threshold, reflecting a sector de-rating in a narrow absolute range rather than index-wide liquidation. From 17:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band at 24 and decays through 23, 22 and 21 into the 20:00 UTC cash close, holds at 20 across the maintenance break and the Globex reopen, and reaches the EA_ON mapping at 19 through the thin mid-Asian hours. It rebuilds to 20, then 21 and 22 as Europe reopens on day one of the two-day policy meeting. A reclaim of 29,000 is the nearest conditional invalidation of the current structure and a fourth lower low beneath 28,833.50 with shallow pullbacks would be the nearest confirmation. Every value beyond the current clock hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
